messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into German, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE German line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑to‑Word Alignment Table (German translation → Italian source)**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Word/Phrase | Back‑Translation | Status | |-------------|----------------------|--------------------|------------------|--------| | Ed | conjunction “And” | **Und** | “and” | OK | | ecco | interjection “lo!” (exclamatory pointer) | **siehe** | “see / behold” | OK | | quasi | adverb “almost” | **fast** | “almost” | OK | | al | preposition + article “at the” | **am** | “at the” (dative) | OK | | cominciar | noun “beginning” | **Anfang** | “beginning” | OK | | de | preposition “of” (genitive marker) | **des** | “of the” (genitive) | OK | | l'erta | noun “the steep (path)” | **steilen Pfades** | “steep path” (genitive) | OK | | una | indefinite article “a” | **eine** | “a” | OK | | lonza | noun “she‑leopard” | **Leopardin** | “she‑leopard” | OK | | leggera | adjective “light” | **leichte** | “light” | OK | | e | coordinating conjunction “and” | **und** | “and” | OK | | presta | adjective “nimble” | **flinke** | “nimble” | OK | | molto | adverb “very” (intensifier) | **sehr** | “very” | OK | | che | relative pronoun “which” | **die** | “which” | OK | | di | preposition “with” | **mit** | “with” | OK | | pel | noun “coat / fur” | **Fell** | “coat / fur” | OK | | macolato | adjective “spotted” | **gef​leckten** | “spotted” | OK | | era | verb “was” (imperf.) | **war** | “was” | OK | | coverta | past participle “covered” | **bedeckt** | “covered” | OK |
### Post‑table notes - **Extra target element:** the German article **„einem“** in the phrase *„mit einem gefleckten Fell“* is required by German grammar but has no direct counterpart in the Italian source. It is therefore an **unavoidable insertion**, not a translation error. - No source words are **MISSING**, **WRONG**, **GRAMMAR**‑incorrect, or **UNNECESSARY** (i.e., omitted because the target language does not need them).

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only German script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final German text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).

- Line 31: - Original: Und siehe fast am Anfang des steilen Pfades, - Issue: none - Corrected: no change - Line 32: - Original: eine leichte und sehr flinke Leopardin, - Issue: none - Corrected: no change - Line 33: - Original: die mit einem gefleckten Fell bedeckt war; - Issue: none - Corrected: no change
